gaps.term: contractions / size of a ring element
gaps.quote: every power of $\omega_t$ preserves their size; each entry is an average of $t$ such images, hence both transforms are contractions (cited)
gaps.note: The page never defines the size (norm) of a ring element or a list of them (the paper uses the maximum modulus of the coefficients, line 2779, and of all coefficients for arrays), nor what a contraction is (a map that does not increase this norm). Without the norm the reader cannot check that a signed shift preserves size, or that an average of t images of norm at most that of z has norm at most that of z.

gaps.quote: Instead the cancellation of sums of powers of $\omega_t$ is verified directly (cited).
gaps.note: The page does not state what the cited result says (for integer j, the sum of omega_t^{jk} over k is t if t divides j and 0 otherwise, so that F_t^+ F_t^- = I/t; paper lines 2810-2817) nor why it is needed, namely that it shows F_t^+ undoes F_t^- up to the factor 1/t. The reader cannot tell what 'cancellation' refers to or what replaces the division.
